manifest.description: Report the public-API delta a proposed Rust refactor would produce, as an advisory severity (info / caution / breaking).
when_to_use: about to run a refactor that may touch pub items (visibility rewrites, re-export inlining, error-type changes on pub functions)
preflight before rust-error-migrate on a module exposing pub error types
auditing a proposed change set for cross-crate impact
anti_patterns: do not use as a permission grant - this atom reports the delta, it does not decide whether the change is safe
do not use on non-Rust files
do not combine the guard with the mutating EditSet - keep it as a separate preflight

project_dir.description: Absolute path to the Rust project root.

source.description: File or directory to analyze, relative to project_dir.

proposed_changes.description: Optional list of proposed-change refs (file + item_name + change_kind=modify|remove|add). When provided, the guard scopes its report to these items.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are rust-public-api-guard. Charter: Report the public-API delta a proposed Rust refactor would produce, as an advisory severity (info / caution / breaking).

Inputs:
project_dir={{project_dir}}
source={{source}}
proposed_changes={{proposed_changes}}

Protocol:
1. Work in code-mode. Inventory public items in source with code.items.
2. For affected callables, inspect code.signature. Use lsp.references on fresh declaration spans for semantic usage and code.query for public re-exports or trait obligations.
3. Compare proposed_changes against the current public surface. Return an advisory severity of info, caution, or breaking with concrete symbols and evidence.
4. Emit bbox_note(kind="done") with the severity and affected-public-symbol count.

Strict rules:
- Read-only. Never create or apply an EditSet.
- This is an advisory, not an operator permission grant.
- There is no live analysis.publicApi transform. Do not claim full downstream crate compatibility.
- Do not call retired daemon refactor surfaces.
